coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No Mauritania-specific rule on household-employer registration found (all hits were Moroccan CNSS). CLEISS lists employer social contributions 2025 but sources disagree on rates and frequency. Nothing new beyond generic; no evidence of a household-specific duty. Related: Saudi-Mauritania domestic-worker recruitment convention (see candidate on recruitment offices).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: FAOLEX document mau138219 (https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/mau138219.pdf) describes ferrailleur licences (temporary/permanent, local/export, artisan variants, buyer/seller categories, 50,000 UM fee, commerce register, criminal record; both parties must show licence on local deals). Date and number not confirmed; PDF is a scanned image that I could not read directly, so currency unverified.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget. No evidence either way.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No jeweller purchase-register rule found. Gold chain is state-run (Maaden, Central Bank, Comptoir National de l'Or, 2016 licence for gold artisans), consistent with K04. Nothing new beyond K04.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or parts-dealer licensing regime found. Only fact: import ban on used vehicles older than 8 years (loi de finances 2010-005, Global Trade Alert; current status unconfirmed). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Large Tabaski export corridor to Senegal (agreement for 450,000 sheep in 2026, Trarza crossing; Senegal duty exemption in 2025). Health certificate required for commercial animal movement (FAO text citing a 1962 law); a one-stop shop for sanitary certification is claimed by a trade expert. No municipal market-fee schedule found. Seasonal and state-facilitated.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No butcher permit text found. Old framework: 1962 law on sanitary inspection of animal-origin foods, 48 h lazaret rest, sworn vet inspector, CNERV lab. ONISPA covers fishery products only (decree 066-2007). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget. No evidence either way.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Decree 2009-102 (6 April 2009) organises veterinary pharmacy: marketing authorisation (AMM) from the livestock minister; wholesale import/sale needs a separate 5-year renewable authorisation (arrete 429 of 31 May 2019 for MARI VET Sarl is an example); changes must be declared to the Direction des Services Veterinaires two months ahead. 2017 arrete governs vet practice; Ordre national des docteurs veterinaires exists. Few licensed firms, so small buyer pool.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Search returned only French and Moroccan sources. No Mauritanian driller licence or abstraction authorisation text found (a 2005 water code is suspected but unconfirmed).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Household waste collection in Nouakchott has been consolidated into large tendered contracts (2025: Moroccan firms SOS NDD / Arma Environnement, sources conflict). Septic emptying: only old studies (about 6 firms in 2001-02), no current authorisation regime found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Mauritanian lift/boiler inspection regime found; only an industrial job post (MEPSI) showing pressure-vessel inspection work exists. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Not searched on its own; the well/drilling search (cat 10) returned nothing for Mauritania. No evidence.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Law 2000-42 on plant protection and a 2002 implementing decree: all phytosanitary products need homologation before import, distribution or use; the Service de la Protection des Vegetaux (SPV, Ministry of Rural Development) grants agrements to manufacturers, importers, distributors and service providers (FAOLEX mau159974 / mau159976, SPV report 2011). Fertiliser rules not found. Sources old; current list of licensed firms not found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Saudi-Mauritanian agreement on recruiting trained Mauritanian domestic workers, with Saudi Musaned-licensed offices already offering Mauritanian workers (date not confirmed). Earlier 2018 bilateral convention and trafficking allegations by CLTM/AFCF/SOS Esclaves. No Mauritanian licensing text for recruitment offices found. Reputation and trafficking risk is high.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No search spent; budget.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Law 2021-004 (March 2021) on associations, foundations and networks: declaration regime replacing 1964 authorisation, minimum five founders, register, financial/accounting/tax control (art. 19 ff.). About 6,000 organisations (2020 press figure, stale). Interior Ministry (DGAT) can suspend associations. Cooperatives and unions are excluded. No halal supervision rule found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: No current licence register text found. Night-time ban on public passenger and freight transport from midnight to 5am (October 2023). Guidebook claims taxis need no licence (undated). 2004-05 reform created a Bureau National des Transports monopoly (older EU case study). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: No communal market-tax digitisation found. Joint order R165/MIDEC/MEF of 20 March 2019 splits taxes between Nouakchott urban community and communes. National e-commerce strategy 2026-2030 (validated Oct 2025) aims to formalise small traders. March 2026 street protests over 30 percent customs duty on smartphones. Money changers: Dec 2023 shift to an interbank FX market; Central Bank studying manual-exchange regulation with Morocco's Office des changes (April 2024); no BCM manual-exchange text found; new banking law of 30 Jan 2025.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nurseries: Ordonnance 2006-048 of 28 Dec 2006 (text read from the Interior Ministry DGAT site): private creches/garderies for ages 0-6 need ministerial authorisation (art. 11), opening conditions set by order (art. 10), fines for opening without it (art. 12), further sanctions and bans (art. 13-14); inspected by early-childhood ministry, local authorities and communal hygiene services. Driving schools: no Mauritanian licensing text found. Tattoo, hunting, small food producers: not searched.

coverage.found: Pharmacy law of 2004 lets any Mauritanian open a pharmacy with a responsible pharmacist; 38 private wholesaler-distributors in 2022 (10 import); CAMEC is the sole importer of some classes. coverage.category: 35. Import registration, customs brokers and importers

candidates.name: Scrap-metal licence holders (ferrailleur) logbook, traceability and licence renewal pack
candidates.trigger: Decree n°2010-140 of 14 June 2010 (Journal Officiel of 15 October 2010, p. 1225-1229): nobody may collect, store, transport, sell or buy scrap without a 'licence de ferrailleur' (TL, TX, PL, PX, plus artisan versions TLA/PLA). Temporary licences last one year and are renewable; both seller and buyer must show their licence in local deals (art. 10); sites and depots not listed in the books kept at the Direction des Mines et de la Geologie are closed (art. 13); a licence can be suspended for lack of traceability of acquisitions (art. 11); losses must be declared within 24 hours (art. 12); exports need a no-objection certificate, purchase invoices and a copy of the licence (art. 10). Fees: TL 1,000,000 old UM, TX 5,000,000, PL 10,000,000, PX 30,000,000 (about 100k to 3M new MRU).
candidates.unchecked: Whether the decree is still applied, how many licence holders exist (likely few, fee is high), whether a purchase register format exists, any newer arrete. The required competitor search (local-language 'logiciel registre ferraille Mauritanie') was not run because the 18-search budget was spent; therefore unverified for competition.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: 3 searches (FR, FR electronics, AR). No Mauritanian rule found on second-hand dealer or pawnbroker registers or police declarations. Only relevant legal text: Law 2022-011 of 15 June 2022 on movable security interests (simplified pledge, retention of title), per the Hogan Lovells note, which does not mention professional pawnbrokers. Nouakchott's 'Noukdha Sakhina' phone market (le360, 2021) is a large second-hand phone trade, but no register duty was confirmed. The one regulated second-hand-adjacent activity is scrap metal (Decree 2010-140, see candidate). Nothing new beyond that; unverified whether any pawn licence exists.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: 3 searches (FR, AR x2) found no Mauritanian funeral-service or cemetery regulation, no commercial funeral operators and no municipal fee schedule. Only anthropological studies on funeral customs. Burial in Mauritania appears to be handled informally by family, mosque and neighbourhood networks, with no sign of a mandatory register or report. Nothing found; not checked: communal (mairie) bylaws and Ministry of Islamic Affairs circulars, which are not online.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: 6 searches (FR, AR, EN) plus 1 fetch. No importer or miller stock-reporting duty found in any source. Context: Mauritania imports roughly 70-90% of its cereals (WFP/OCHA, older); Grands Moulins de Mauritanie and Wafa Holding's mill dominate milling (60-70% local share, 2021), so buyers are large, not small. The state Commissariat a la Securite Alimentaire (CSA) runs stocks and subsidised shops (Emel plan 2012); a China-financed 30,000 t Nouakchott warehouse for the CSA was agreed on 28 May 2025 (foodbusinessmea, 3 June 2025) with no rules on traders. SONIMEX is the state import-export company. Gum arabic: grown in Trarza, Brakna and Gorgol, with a chain of collector, trader and exporter (UNCTAD); World Bank SAWAP project there; no licensing rule found. Coffee and cocoa not applicable. Not checked: ministry of commerce import-licence regime for rice, wheat and sugar; current CSA rules.

result.reason: A FAOLEX decree exists (scanned, search-summary only). It bans collecting, storing, transporting, selling or buying scrap without a ferrailleur licence. The licence is temporary (1 year, renewable) or permanent, local or export, and costs 50,000 UM. It is issued by joint ministerial order, and the file needs a commerce register entry and a clean record. I could not confirm the decree number, date, whether it is still in force, or any periodic register or reporting duty. The fetch returned only unreadable PDF data. Arabic and French searches found no competitor and no recent news. No count of licensees was found, and the trade is likely small and informal. The duty is a one-off licence renewal, not a recurring workflow. Buyers are few, informal and unlikely to pay. Low score.

Law 2024-045 of 18 Dec 2024 is confirmed. Operators and first-tier subcontractors must file three-year plans and annual reports, and a digital platform is planned (Financial Afrik, Lextenso). Pinsent Masons says regulations were adopted in Sept 2025 and companies must register local hiring and procurement via an online portal. I found no decree text, deadlines, penalty amounts or evidence the portal is live. No private competitor found. First-tier subcontractors are probably mid-size or large, and the state portal likely covers the filing, so the market is small and a private tool is hard to justify. I did not run a French or Arabic software-vendor search. Score 3.

CLEISS says CNSS affiliation has been compulsory for Labour Code employees since Feb 2021. A decree of 29 Oct 2009 requires a work permit for foreign workers. I couldn't open either text, and found no penalty or frequency figures. Searches found no Mauritanian CNSS e-filing portal or dedicated competitor. Results were mostly Moroccan Damancom pages. The duty is mostly one-off registration, plus monthly CNSS returns, which is generic payroll and out of scope. The foreign-worker permit niche is tiny and an informal-economy market. It is close to rejected K03. Buyers would likely rely on accountants. No market count was found. Low score.

The duty exists but does not fall on agents as a filing workflow. Payspace says the 0.1% tax is levied by the payment operator, and transactions under 5,000 MRU and payments to the Treasury and CNSS are exempt. The 10% on agent commissions looks like a deduction at source, so agents probably have no recurring return to file. Agents struck for three days in February 2026 over the taxes (Le360), so this is a political issue, not a software task. I could not read the Orbitax article beyond its excerpt. I did not find the Finance Act text, the filing deadlines, the penalties or the number of agents. I did not search for competitors, so that part is unchecked. A July 2026 amending finance law may have changed the rules, and I did not check it.

result.competitor: None found. Closest: state SSPAC catch-monitoring system and paper licences from the fisheries ministry (MPEM).
result.duty: Pirogue registration, an annual artisanal licence naming foreign crew, and per-trip declaration. Penalty not confirmed.
result.market: About 6,200 to 7,500 Mauritanian-flag pirogues by some sources; 20,689 registered with 10,592 licences in an undated Senegalese source.
result.reason: The duty is real but old and thinly sourced. The 2022 licence split (55,000 and 65,500 MRU) and the 2017 rule naming foreign crew on the licence come from Le360 articles. Pirogues must be registered, hold a licence, and declare trips; the trip rule rests on an old testimony. Licences are secure paper under ministry orders (2016 arrêté), and I found no electronic licence portal. I found no competing software. Catch data is collected by state field surveys (SSPAC) and plant-issued daily slips. A solo founder faces weak buyer fit: licences are annual, the buyers are low-literacy owners with low willingness to pay, and the state owns the registry. Fleet counts run from about 6,200 to 20,689 pirogues, depending on source and date. I did not confirm current licence rules or penalties.
